title: Quasi-finiteness at a prime descends to an intermediate ring
statement: Let $A\to B$ and $B\to C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings such that the composite $A\to C$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] (then $B\to C$ is of finite type). Let $\mathfrak r\subset C$ be a prime ideal. If $A\to C$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak r$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], then $B\to C$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak r$.

proof.text: FiniteType.of_restrictScalars_finiteType A B C supplies finite type over B from finite type over A [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

Put p = r ∩ A and q = r ∩ B. Use PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber (Mathlib/RingTheory/LocalRing/ResidueField/Fiber.lean:212), the topological form of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection], to identify Spec of each fibre ring with its fibre subspace in Spec C [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Pull back the open singleton in the hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] along the A-fibre homeomorphism; injectivity identifies this preimage with the singleton at r.

The fibre over q includes into the fibre over p: IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq and PrimeSpectrum.comap_comp_apply show that a prime contracting to q in B contracts to p in A. The inclusion is continuous by continuous_subtype_val.subtype_mk, and its preimage of the singleton at r is the singleton at r by Subtype.ext. Pull back the open singleton and transport openness along the B-fibre homeomorphism. This is exactly [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] over B.

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks Algebra 0C6H in 4 steps: (1) B → C of finite type from the generators of C over A (00F4, elementary); (2) the ring map θ: C⊗_Aκ(p) → C⊗_Bκ(q), c⊗λ ↦ c⊗λ̄, with θ∘j_A = j_B, written out from the A-balanced map (elementary, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime); (3) by lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection (Mathlib leaf) applied to A → C and to B → C, Q ↦ θ^{-1}(Q) pulls the point r̄_A back to exactly {r̄_B}; (4) Spec θ is continuous, so {r̄_B} is open, which is the DAG's definition of quasi-finite at r. The source argues with 00PK (3) (D(c) ∩ primes over p = {r}); since the DAG's definition is 00PK (1) and no node states (1)⇔(3) or that Spec of the fibre ring is homeomorphic to the fibre, the subset argument is realized by θ, needing no new node (proof_origin agent, document 0C6H).
